summary: Deletes the old customer_session_codes database table (one-time customer-portal sign-in codes) and its model; nothing in the app used it anymore since sign-in codes moved to the email OTP flow. Also removes it from an on-call secret-rotation SQL check.

statements.why: The table is unused by app code at both 3bb3fab6~1 and 3bb3fab6 (only the model file referenced it); dropping it holds only short-lived (30 min) login codes. No security/money issue.

statements.text: Most of this change is in a new file, server/migrations/versions/2026-10-30-0800_drop_customer_session_codes.py (109 lines added).
statements.why: True that the migration is the bulk (stat says 118 lines, not 109 — minor). Says nothing about what it does.
Removed one line from an internal on-call SQL check.

statements.text: Apply the migration to your live database before the new code goes live (`alembic upgrade head`), or the parts that use it will fail.
statements.why: Running the migration is needed, but no code uses the table before or after this commit, so nothing fails if code ships first; for a table drop, code-first is the normal safe order.

statements.text: Back up your data first: the migration deletes data and can't be undone.
statements.why: drop_table deletes rows; downgrade recreates an empty table. Data is only expired/short-lived login codes, so low stakes, but the statement is true.

misses.what: Never says in plain words what is removed: an old, already-unused table of customer-portal sign-in codes (replaced by the email OTP flow), so customer sign-in is unaffected.
